explanations.answer: Men from thirty to fifty years old
explanations.explanation: Thirty to fifty, friend. That's the range the LORD gives Moses and Aaron for everyone qualified to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 4:3). It comes up again for each clan, so it's no accident. If somebody asked me my age to get in, I'd have nothing to say, because I don't have one.

explanations.answer: Men from twenty to sixty years old
explanations.explanation: That's a wider net than the LORD casts here. The text says thirty to fifty, and it says it for the Kohathites and again for the other clans. Twenty to sixty has a nice round ring to it, I'll give you that. But the number in this passage is thirty to fifty.

explanations.answer: Men twenty years old or more
explanations.explanation: That would pull in a lot more men, and I get the thinking. But the LORD tells Moses and Aaron thirty to fifty for this work (Numbers 4:3). Fifty is the other end of the range, so there's a stopping point too. It's a range with two ends, like a cookie timer that dings when it's done.

Carrying it is. First Aaron and his sons cover the holy objects, and only then do the Kohathites come and do the carrying (Numbers 4:15). One group wraps and another group hauls. In my bakery I do both jobs with one mustache, and you can tell by the boxes.

The wrapping is already done by the time the Kohathites show up. Aaron and his sons go in and cover the holy objects (Numbers 4:5). Then the Kohathites come to do the carrying. It's like walking into a kitchen after the dough is already mixed, and your job is the oven.

Counting was the first job in this passage, and it wasn't theirs. The LORD told Moses and Aaron to take the census of the Kohathites (Numbers 4:2). So the Kohathites get counted, and they don't do the counting. When the camp is ready to move, they come and do the carrying (Numbers 4:15). They're the chocolate chips in this recipe, not the one counting them.

I can see why careful sounds safe, friend. But the verse doesn't leave room for it. It says, “But they must not touch the holy objects, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:15). So the Kohathites carry, and the touching is something they don't do.

False, and the text is plain about it. “But they must not touch the holy objects, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:15). Being careful isn't part of the verse at all. That's why the objects are covered first and carried with poles and a carrying frame (Numbers 4:5-15).

explanations.answer: The entire tabernacle and everything in it
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest, has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy objects and their utensils (Numbers 4:16). The oil, the incense and the grain offering are only part of his job. That's a lot to keep track of. I can barely keep track of one apron.

explanations.answer: The training of the men for battle
explanations.explanation: Nothing about battle shows up in Eleazar's job here. The text lists the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the daily grain offering and the anointing oil. Then it adds that he has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it (Numbers 4:16). Eleazar is Aaron's son and a priest, and his work is tabernacle work.

explanations.answer: The food and water for the whole camp
explanations.explanation: The whole camp is a big job, and this verse doesn't hand it to Eleazar. His oversight is the oil, the incense, the daily grain offering and the anointing oil. After that, the verse says he has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it (Numbers 4:16). Eleazar is Aaron's son and a priest, and his job stays at the tabernacle.

explanations.answer: Go in and assign each man his task
explanations.explanation: Yes. Aaron and his sons go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry (Numbers 4:19). The LORD gives this so the Kohathites may live and not die when they come near the most holy things. Nobody has to guess what to grab. It's like a boss who hands out the jobs before anybody picks up anything.

explanations.answer: Teach them to wrap the holy objects
explanations.explanation: The wrapping is Aaron and his sons' own work. They go in and cover the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altars themselves (Numbers 4:5-14). What the LORD asks for the Kohathites in verse 19 is different. Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry.

explanations.answer: Lead them in carrying only at night
explanations.explanation: Night never comes up in this passage. Not once, friend. The LORD says Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry (Numbers 4:19). That's the help the Kohathites get.

True. The LORD says, “But the Kohathites are not to go in and look at the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:20). That's a serious line, and it's meant to be. It also sits right beside the LORD's care for them. He had just said he wants them to live and not die when they come near the most holy things (Numbers 4:19).

It's the other way around, friend. The LORD says, “But the Kohathites are not to go in and look at the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.” (Numbers 4:20). That's a serious line. It comes right after He says He wants them to live and not die when they come near the most holy things (Numbers 4:19).

That's it. The Gershonites carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, the entrance curtains and the courtyard curtains (Numbers 4:25-26). Their ropes and equipment go along too. That's a whole lot of fabric. I'd be lost in the first fold.

The Gershonite list has nothing like shields or spears on it. It's all curtains. They carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, and the curtains of the courtyard, along with their ropes (Numbers 4:25-26). This is carrying work for the Tent of Meeting.

Trumpets and banners aren't on the Gershonites' list. What is on it? The curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, the entrance curtains and the courtyard curtains, plus their ropes (Numbers 4:25-26). If you want a sound out of this job, listen for a lot of folding.

I can see why you'd say that, friend, but the text says otherwise. All the Gershonites' work is to be done at the direction of Aaron and his sons. The LORD tells Moses, “you are to assign to them all that they are responsible to carry.” (Numbers 4:27). So the assigning comes from above them, and the men don't pick their own loads.

False. All the Gershonites' service is done at the direction of Aaron and his sons (Numbers 4:27). The LORD tells Moses, “you are to assign to them all that they are responsible to carry.” Nobody gets to grab the lightest curtain and run. I'd have been first in line for that, no question.

That's right. The Merarites carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts and bases. They also carry the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and ropes (Numbers 4:31-32). Every piece matters when a tent has to go up again. I lose a single pen in a junk drawer, so I'd never survive this job.

No music on this one. The Merarites carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts and bases (Numbers 4:31). They also carry the courtyard posts with their bases, tent pegs and ropes (Numbers 4:32). It's hauling work, from frames to pegs.

Baskets and sacks don't show up in the Merarites' list. What does? The frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts and bases (Numbers 4:31). Then the courtyard posts with their bases, tent pegs and ropes (Numbers 4:32). Those are the things that hold the tent up and in place.

explanations.answer: Each item is assigned by name
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says, “You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.” (Numbers 4:32). With that many pieces, a name on every item means no confusion. Nobody has to wonder whose peg that is. I wish my kitchen drawers ran like that.

explanations.answer: Each man picks what he wants
explanations.explanation: That would get messy fast, wouldn't it? The text says something else. The LORD says, “You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.” (Numbers 4:32). The items are assigned by name, so the men don't choose them.

Lots don't come up anywhere in this passage, friend. The way the LORD tells Moses to do it is clear. “You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.” (Numbers 4:32). Every item goes with a name.

True. Ithamar, Aaron's son and a priest, directs both clans. The Gershonites' duties are under his direction (Numbers 4:28), and so is the work of the Merarites (Numbers 4:33). One director, two clans. That's a big stack of tent gear for one man to keep track of.

It's actually the same man for both. Ithamar, Aaron's son and a priest, directs the Gershonites (Numbers 4:28). The Merarites' work is also under the direction of Ithamar (Numbers 4:33). So he has a lot on his plate, and I bet he stayed busy.

That's not what the text says. It counts all three clans, Kohathites, Gershonites and Merarites, and they total 8,580 men (Numbers 4:46-48). Then it says, “…each one was assigned his work and burden, as the LORD had commanded Moses.” (Numbers 4:49). So the work goes to every counted man, and it doesn't stop at one clan.

False. All three clans are counted, and the Levites total 8,580 men (Numbers 4:46-48). Then the text says, “…each one was assigned his work and burden, as the LORD had commanded Moses.” (Numbers 4:49). Each one means each one. Every counted man gets a job, and that's about the best news a man can hear.
